verdictSummary: NOT a planner defect. Both flagged blueprints are correct. The `sheet-header-safety` tier-0 check gates on APP NAME alone (`app in {google sheets, airtable, notion}`) and never inspects the action, so it demands a `headers` parameter from every Notion step including standalone PAGE creation. Rule 6's own trigger clause is narrower than the check that claims to enforce it.
problem: The `sheet-header-safety` tier-0 check gates on app name alone and fails every Notion step regardless of action — producing 2 false failures (ctfm-01, msh-03) out of 8 sheet/table steps in the eval set, a 25% false-positive rate on this criterion, while both flagged blueprints are schema-correct Notion writes that carry no positional row data (tier0_code_checks.py:69-70).

checkImplementation.quote:
sheet_apps = {"google sheets", "airtable", "notion"}
relevant_steps = [s for s in steps if (s.get("app") or "").strip().lower() in sheet_apps]
...
missing = [s["step_number"] for s in relevant_steps if "headers" not in (s.get("parameters") or {})]
checkImplementation.whatHappened: The filter keys on `s['app']` ONLY. It never reads `s['action']`. Any step whose app string is 'Notion' — a page create, a database row add, even a read — is classified as a structured row write and must carry a literal `headers` key.
checkImplementation.divergenceFromItsOwnCriterion: agentspec.yaml defines the criterion as "Any step writing row(s) of structured data into a spreadsheet/table/database includes a headers parameter." The code implements "any step whose APP is Notion/Sheets/Airtable". The code is strictly broader than the criterion it claims to enforce — an app-level gate used as a proxy for an action-level condition.

rule6ExactWording.triggerClauseQuote: Whenever a step writes row(s) of structured data into a spreadsheet/table/database (Google Sheets, Airtable, a Notion database, ...)
rule6ExactWording.mechanismClauseQuote: Many of these tools otherwise treat the very first row of data as the column headers instead of storing it, silently discarding what should have been real data — this is true even for a SINGLE row, which would otherwise be entirely lost.
rule6ExactWording.orderingClauseQuote: the execution engine turns a single JSON object into one row with one cell per field, in the same order as `headers`.
rule6ExactWording.analysis: The mechanism clause is decisive and it is NOT ambiguous: the harm Rule 6 prevents is a POSITIONAL append pathology — an ordered array of values whose columns are inferred from the first row. The ordering clause ("in the same order as `headers`") confirms Rule 6 presupposes ORDER-dependent, positionally-addressed writes. Notion's create-database-page is KEY-ADDRESSED: `properties` is a dict whose KEYS ARE the column names, so there is no first row to consume and no order to preserve. Rule 6's stated harm is structurally impossible for both flagged steps.
rule6ExactWording.residualAmbiguity: REAL BUT SECONDARY, and it affects ctfm-01 only. Rule 6's trigger clause names "a Notion database" in its in-scope example list while its mechanism clause describes a pathology Notion cannot exhibit. A literal reader who stops at the trigger clause could wrongly conclude `headers` is required for NOTION_CREATE_DATABASE_PAGE. The planner did NOT make that error — it read the mechanism clause correctly and emitted the schema-correct key-addressed shape. This is a clarity gap worth closing, NOT the root cause of the 2 failures.

remedies.title: Narrow sheet-header-safety from an app-name gate to a write-shape gate
remedies.description: Replace the app-only filter in check_sheet_header_safety with a gate on the WRITE SHAPE: the criterion fires only when a step performs a POSITIONAL row append (action verb ADD_ROW / APPEND_ROW / INSERT_ROW / CREATE_ROW / ADD_RECORD / CREATE_RECORD / BATCH_UPDATE) AND the payload is not key-addressed (no populated `properties` dict). Notion page creation then correctly resolves to n/a while every genuine Google Sheets / Airtable row append is still checked. Fix the instrument, not the planner — the planner's output was right on both traces.
remedies.rationale: The check's own criterion in agentspec.yaml reads "Any step writing row(s) of structured data", but the code selects on app name alone and never reads s['action']. ctfm-01 (key-addressed properties, column names already in the payload) and msh-03 (free-text page body, zero structured fields) both trip it while being schema-correct. A check faithful to its criterion would return n/a on both.
remedies.whyWorks: The false positives come from one specific over-broad predicate. Gating on the action verb removes non-row-write actions, and exempting a populated `properties` dict removes key-addressed writes — exactly the two shapes in which Rule 6's stated harm (first row silently consumed as headers) is structurally impossible. Replay over all 8 sheet/table steps in the eval set confirms only ctfm-01 and msh-03 change verdict (fail -> n/a); all 6 genuine positional row writes still pass, so no detection power is lost.

If an Airtable or Sheets action ever emits a populated `properties` dict for a genuinely positional write, it would be wrongly exempted; the action-verb gate is the primary filter and no such case exists in the current eval set.

remedies.title: Close Rule 6's page-vs-row clarity gap with an explicit key-addressed exception
remedies.description: OPTIONAL hardening, not the root-cause fix. Rule 6's trigger clause lists "a Notion database" as in-scope while its mechanism clause describes a positional pathology Notion cannot exhibit. The planner resolved this correctly on both traces, so this is a latent readability risk rather than an observed defect. Add an explicit exception naming key-addressed property writes and standalone page creation so a literal reader cannot reach the wrong conclusion.

exactChange.beforeSummary: Rule 6 (Headers for Spreadsheet/Table Row Writes): Whenever a step writes row(s) of structured data into a spreadsheet/table/database (Google Sheets, Airtable, a Notion database, ...) — whether it's a Rule 5 fan-out (many rows) or a single record ...
exactChange.after: Rule 6 (Headers for Spreadsheet/Table Row Writes): Whenever a step appends row(s) of structured data POSITIONALLY into a spreadsheet/table (Google Sheets, Airtable, ...) — i.e. the row is a bare ordered list of values and the tool infers the columns from whatever it sees first — whether it's a Rule 5 fan-out (many rows) or a single record ... ALWAYS also include a `headers` parameter alongside the row data. EXCEPTION — do NOT add `headers` when the target action is KEY-ADDRESSED, i.e. the payload already names its own columns (e.g. a Notion database page, whose `properties` object carries the column names as keys: `{"Status": "In Progress", "Priority": "High"}`), or when the step creates a standalone PAGE or document whose body is free text rather than a row of fields (e.g. NOTION_CREATE_PAGE with a `content` blob). In both cases there is no first-row to be silently consumed, and a `headers` parameter is not part of the target's real schema.

remedies.rationale: Rule 6 says "a Notion database" is in scope, yet its mechanism clause ("treat the very first row of data as the column headers") and its ordering clause ("in the same order as `headers`") both presuppose positional addressing that a Notion `properties` dict does not use. The two clauses point opposite ways for NOTION_CREATE_DATABASE_PAGE. No trace shows the planner getting this wrong, so the gap is latent, not active.
remedies.whyWorks: Naming the exception makes the mechanism clause's implicit scope explicit at the point of the trigger clause, so a reader never has to infer scope from the harm description. It also pre-empts the opposite failure — a future planner revision adding a bogus `headers` array to a Notion page write, which the execution engine's schema-alignment layer would then have to strip.

remedies.title: Restate the criterion description so code and spec agree on scope
remedies.description: The agentspec criterion description and its implementation disagree: the description says "Any step writing row(s) of structured data", the code says "any step whose app is Notion/Sheets/Airtable". Even after R-shs-1 the prose still fails to state the positional/key-addressed distinction, leaving the same drift free to reappear on the next re-implementation.

exactChange.before: Any step writing row(s) of structured data into a spreadsheet/table/database includes a headers parameter.
exactChange.after: Any step that appends row(s) of structured data POSITIONALLY into a spreadsheet/table (Google Sheets, Airtable) includes a headers parameter. Key-addressed writes whose payload already names its own columns (e.g. a Notion database page's `properties` object) and standalone page/document creation are OUT OF SCOPE and score n/a.

remedies.rationale: The criterion prose is the contract the code-check implements. Because the prose omits the positional qualifier, the app-name shortcut in tier0_code_checks.py:69-70 reads as a faithful implementation, which is how the over-broad gate survived review in the first place.
remedies.whyWorks: Writing the scope boundary into the criterion removes the ambiguity that licensed the app-name shortcut, so any future re-implementation inherits the narrowed semantics and the n/a case is specified rather than inferred.
